title.narrative: Deepening Access via Rural Electrification (DARE): Providing energy services to underserved communities in Belize

description.narrative: There is a strong correlation between poverty and access to basic services and amenities. As part of Belize’s National Energy Policy (2023-2040), the country aims to provide “Universal access to basic services and improved access to modern services.’ Although 90% of Belize’s population has access to a reliable source of electricity many persons within rural communities across the country do not have access to modern forms of energy. In fact, of the 27 registered villages without access to electricity, 24 are found within the Toledo District alone. The “Rural Electrification using Microgrids in Southern Belize” project proposal was approved by the Board of Directors of India, Brazil and South Africa Facility for Poverty and Hunger Alleviation (IBSA Fund), and aims to address the critical needs of the marginalized communities within the 3 villages of Mabil-Ha, Otoxha, and Na Luum Caj in the Toledo District in Belize, for access to electricity. These communities face significant socioeconomic challenges, including a lack of access to electricity. Through this project, the Ministry of Rural Transformation, Community Development, Labour & Local Government of Belize (MRTCDLLG) seeks to improve the quality of life in these communities by providing solar panels, with charge controllers, battery banks and inverters, for electricity generation. This project will also contribute to, and build on, the work of the Ministry of Public Utilities, Energy, Logistics & E-Governance (MPUELE) as it relates to their “Rural Electrification Project” and will utilize female solar engineers who were trained by the Government of India via a South-South exchange programme. The main objective of this project is to promote rural electrification through isolated solar photovoltaic systems as a low-carbon and resilient development strategy for rural communities in Toledo, Belize.
